stage1Hint1: Count the cells between the robot and the star.

rotation.1: Add a right turn and run it.

repeat.1: Select repeat and choose to put blocks inside.

condition.1: The sensor checks the square ahead.
condition.2: A wall ahead makes the turn inside if run.
condition.3: With an open square ahead, if skips its body.
condition.alt1: There is a wall ahead of the robot. The blocked-ahead check is true.
condition.alt2: The path ahead was blocked, so the right turn inside if ran.
condition.alt3: The path ahead is open, so the check is false and the turn inside if was skipped.

else.1: Choose else as the place to add blocks.
else.3: With an open square ahead, only else runs.
else.alt3: The path ahead is open, so the check is false. Only the left turn in else ran.

while.1: The path is clear, so move one square.
while.3: A wall stops while without entering its body.
while.alt1: The path ahead was clear, so the check was true and the robot moved one square.
while.alt2: The path ahead is still clear on the next check, so the result is true.
while.alt3: There is now a wall ahead, so the check is false. The loop stopped without entering its body.

function.0: Create a function and open its star card.
function.1: Put a turn inside the star function.
function.2: Return to main and call the star function.
function.3: Run the star body, then return after the call.

variable.1: Choose A as the repeat count source.
variable.2: The value 3 passes from A to repeat.
variable.3: Turn as many times as A says.
variable.alt1: The value 3 in box A is selected as the repeat count.
variable.alt2: Box A holds 3, and the repeat count is also 3.
variable.alt3: The right turn ran three times, using the value 3 in box A.

logic.0: Select if to edit its condition.
logic.1: Choose left to check the wall on that side.
logic.2: Turn on not to change false to true.
logic.3: Choosing and or or shows two condition slots.
logic.alt2: The left side is open. Negating the false left-blocked check makes it true.
logic.alt3: The two checks ask whether the left side and the path ahead are blocked. Both are open, so both checks and their combined and result are false.

parameter.1: Use ◆ for the repeat count inside the function.
parameter.2: Choose 2 as the number to send in the call.
parameter.alt0: The star function has an input for a number.
parameter.alt1: The repeat count inside the star function uses its input number.
parameter.alt2: The number to send to the star function is 2. Box A holds 4.
parameter.alt3: The star function received input 2 and repeated twice. Box A still holds 4.

return.0: Add return inside the function and choose 2.
return.1: Use the function result for the main repeat count.
return.2: The function sends 2 back with return.
return.3: Skip the turn after return and continue main.
return.alt0: The value for the star function to return is 2.
return.alt1: The repeat count in main uses the value returned by the star function.
return.alt2: The star function returned 2. The right turn after return is skipped.
return.alt3: Main used the returned value 2 to move forward twice. The turn after return in the function did not run.

event.0: Create an on handler for the diamond signal.
event.2: The diamond signal arrives and waits in the queue.
event.3: Run the connected on body, then finish.
event.alt0: A handler is connected to the diamond signal.
event.alt1: The diamond signal handler contains a right turn.
event.alt2: The diamond signal arrived and entered the queue. It is connected to the diamond handler.
event.alt3: The right turn in the handler connected to the diamond signal ran, then finished.

list.0: Add a list loop and choose its body.
list.1: Use the current value ▣ for the inner repeat count.
list.2: The first element has index 0 and value ▣ of 2.
list.3: The next element has index 1 and value ▣ of 3.
list.alt1: The inner repeat uses the current list value as its count. The list holds 2 and 3.
list.alt2: The current element is at index 0 and its value is 2.
list.alt3: The current element moved to index 1 and its value is 3.

search.0: Choose the comparison body as the place to add blocks.
search.1: Put a stop block inside the condition.
search.2: The value matches target 8, so stop the list loop.
search.3: Leave the remaining slots unchecked and run the next action.
search.alt0: The list holds 5, 2, and 8, and the target is 8. Search starts from the end.
search.alt1: A stop block is placed to stop the loop when the current value matches target 8.
search.alt2: The target is 8. It was found at index 2; indexes 0 and 1 were not checked.
search.alt3: Target 8 was found at index 2 and the loop stopped. Indexes 0 and 1 were not checked, and the forward action after the loop ran.
